question.text: The six-step financial planning process begins with which of the following steps?

answer.text: Establishing and defining the client-planner relationship
Developing and presenting financial planning recommendations

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 28 of the workbook lists the six-step financial planning process and states that the process begins when the client engages the Investment Adviser and establishes/defines the client-planner relationship — this happens before any data gathering. The Trap: Gathering client data feels like a natural first move, but the scope and terms of the engagement must be set first; data collection is the second step. Note: The remaining steps in the six-step process build on this first step — analysing the data, developing recommendations, implementing them, and monitoring.
